title: Haydn's The Creation at Symphony Hall, Nov. 5-7
dek: The Boston Symphony Orchestra and Philippe Jordan perform Haydn's oratorio Nov. 5, 6 and 7 at Symphony Hall on Massachusetts Avenue.
body: Joseph Haydn's oratorio The Creation, based on the Genesis story, returns to Boston: this week the Boston Symphony Orchestra brings it to Symphony Hall for the first time since 1998.
## The work and the cast

Haydn composed The Creation late in his life for soloists, chorus and orchestra, drawing on the Genesis account of the world's making. The BSO places it at the opening of a two-part Creation festival that runs through Nov. 14, part of its season-long exploration of faith and spirituality in music.

Philippe Jordan conducts. Three soloists make their BSO debuts: soprano Louise Alder, tenor Bogdan Volkov and bass-baritone David Steffens. The Tanglewood Festival Chorus, prepared by Jean-Sébastien Vallée, the BSO's Director of Choruses, carries the great choral moments. The text is sung in German with English supertitles, so there is no need to know the language.
## Dates and times
There are three performances at Symphony Hall: Thursday, Nov. 5 at 7:30 p.m.; Friday, Nov. 6 at 1:30 p.m.; and Saturday, Nov. 7 at 8 p.m.

Each night has a companion event, with its own separate ticket. On Thursday, Robert Hazen and Mike Wong give a 6:30 p.m. talk titled Time's Second Arrow in the Cabot-Cahners Room. On Friday, Teresa Neff offers a half-hour talk at 12:15 p.m. in the hall. On Saturday, Christian Wiman and Tracy K. Smith give a 6:30 p.m. reading in the Cabot-Cahners Room.
## Tickets

Symphony Hall is at 301 Massachusetts Avenue, Boston. The BSO lists single-ticket links for each performance on its event page, though it does not publish single-ticket prices there. Subscription packages that include this concert start at $231 and run up to the thousands, depending on the series and seats. For help, call the BSO ticketing office at 617-266-1200 (Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Saturday, 12:30 to 4:30 p.m.) or email customerservice@bso.org.
The BSO's next orchestral concerts pair this oratorio with a brand-new work, the Golijov Creation.

title: Arlington Open Studios Brings 80 Local Artists to Town Hall and Maple Street
dek: Saturday, November 7 from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at Arlington Town Hall, the Arlington Community Center and Robbins Library in Arlington.
body: Arlington Center for the Arts presents the 28th annual Arlington Open Studios on Saturday, November 7, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., a town-wide showcase of work by more than 80 local artists. Painters, photographers, fiber artists, ceramicists, glass artists, jewelers, printmakers and sculptors all take part, and most visitors can buy work directly and meet the people who made it.

The day spreads across three connected stops. Arlington Town Hall, at 730 Massachusetts Avenue, has more than 40 artists on two floors, and the Arlington High School Band plays on the Town Hall steps from noon to 4 p.m. The Arlington Community Center and the Arlington Center for the Arts, at 27 Maple Street, hold a second group of more than 40 artists on the ground and first floors, plus a ceramics demonstration from noon to 4 p.m. in the ACA Clay Studio. Robbins Library, at 700 Massachusetts Avenue, adds live readings from the Red Letter Poets.
## Galleries, puppets and food

Two exhibitions give the day a second layer. The Shaira Ali Gallery shows "Opposites Attract," and the Hallway Gallery shows "Inside ACA." Puppet performances by Margaret Moody and friends are scheduled for younger visitors, and The Roasted Granola sells food at the Maple Street entrance. Admission is no charge.

A town-wide open studio day is one of the best ways to meet the artists behind the work you see on gallery walls. The day falls on a single Saturday, so it is worth mapping out which buildings to see before you set out.

title: Igor Levit Brings an All-Beethoven Recital to Symphony Hall
dek: Sunday, Nov. 8 from 3 to 5 p.m. at Symphony Hall, 301 Massachusetts Ave., Back Bay.
body: Pianist Igor Levit makes his Symphony Hall recital debut on Sunday, November 8, with an all-Beethoven program that the presenter, Vivo Performing Arts, describes as a portrait of the composer's inner life. The recital runs from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m.

The program traces a path from the young Beethoven's confident swagger, through the despair that came with his encroaching deafness, to a moment of reprieve and the Waldstein Sonata. That sonata, written around 1803 and 1804 and dedicated to the patron Count Ferdinand Ernst von Waldstein, is one of the composer's most ambitious works for piano and a staple of the repertoire.

Levit has performed with the Boston Symphony Orchestra before, but this is his first recital in Symphony Hall under the Vivo banner. The listing frames the afternoon as a statement of faith in the power of art, and an all-Beethoven program lets listeners follow one composer's arc from beginning to end.
## Getting Tickets

The listing does not spell out every work on the program, so check the event page for the complete set before you go. Single tickets went on sale in August, and Vivo's Applause Circle membership offers early access to tickets. Details, availability and the program are at https://www.vivoperformingarts.org/productions/igor-levit-2026
Symphony Hall is in Back Bay, a short walk from Symphony station on the Green Line. Arrive a little early to find your seat and enjoy the hall before the first note.

title: Poiesis Quartet Plays Beethoven and Prokofiev at the Gardner, Nov. 8
dek: Sunday, Nov. 8, from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. in Calderwood Hall at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, 25 Evans Way in the Fenway.
body: The Poiesis Quartet performs in Calderwood Hall at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum on Sunday, Nov. 8, from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. The concert is part of the museum's Fall 2026 Weekend Concert Series, which runs on select Sundays from Sept. 13 through Nov. 22.
## The program

The listing names four works: Beethoven's final string quartet, Prokofiev's String Quartet No. 1, Sky Macklay's Many Many Cadences, and Tapestry of the Beloved Beatified by Jeff Scott, which the listing describes as a new commission. The mix runs from Beethoven's last quartet to a new commission, a span of about two centuries.
## The ensemble

The quartet was founded in 2022. According to the event listing, The New York Times named it among the best classical performances of 2025, and the group has quickly drawn attention in classical music.
## The hall and the series

Calderwood Hall is a 300-seat room, and the listing notes that about 80 percent of its seats are front row. The Weekend Concert Series dates to 1927 and, according to the listing, is the longest-running museum music program in the country. The concert fills most of a Sunday afternoon, and the listing gives the address as 25 Evans Way, Boston, MA 02115.
## Tickets and details

Tickets are listed at $70 to $99. Seniors pay $63 to $89, and students and children ages 5 to 17 pay $25. The museum's listing for the concert is at gardnermuseum.org/calendar/poiesis-quartet-20261108. Visitors who want the full set of details can also find them on the Boston Calendar page for the concert, which repeats the start and end times.

title: Handmade for the Holidays at Gore Place Brings 60 Makers to Waltham
dek: Sunday, Nov. 8, from 10:00 a.m. at Gore Place, 52 Gore Street in Waltham, rain or shine.
body: Gore Place, the 19th-century estate at 52 Gore Street in Waltham, hosts its Handmade for the Holidays market on Sunday, Nov. 8. The listing describes 60 handmade vendors whom it calls local artisans, and it says the market runs rain or shine.
## Shopping and the grounds

The market is a chance to shop early for holiday gifts, and visitors can also walk the grounds of the estate. The listing does not say which products the vendors sell. It says the market runs rain or shine, so visitors can plan on it going ahead in any weather. The event is a way to combine holiday shopping with a visit to a historic estate.
## Animals and access
The listing notes that visitors can walk the grounds of the 19th-century estate and see heritage breed sheep on the property. Dogs are not permitted on the grounds, but service pets are welcome.
## Hours
The listing gives 10:00 a.m. as the start time. It shows the end time as 2:00 p.m. in one field and 3:00 p.m. in the description, so check with the venue before you go.
## Admission
The listing shows attendance at no charge, and the market is open to the public.

title: Harboring Creativity Brings More Than 20 Artists to ICA Watershed
dek: Sunday, Nov. 8, from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at ICA Watershed, 256 Marginal St., East Boston.
body: The fourth annual Harboring Creativity exhibit and sale, hosted by the East Boston Artists Group, fills ICA Watershed with work by more than 20 local artists. Sunday's hours run from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
## What's on view

Visitors will find original paintings, photography, mixed media, sculpture, jewelry and fiber art. The listing says the pieces are available for purchase, which gives visitors a way to take home work made by people in the neighborhood.
## Meet the artists

A Meet the Artists reception was listed for Saturday, Nov. 7, from 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. The listing describes the show as a way to browse original art, meet the artists and support East Boston's creative community.
## For families

The listing describes the exhibit as family-friendly and lists it as suitable for groups, kids and rainy days. Admission is at no charge and open to all, so it works well as a small outing for a family or a group of friends.
## Where to find it
The listing gives the Sunday hours as 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and places the show at ICA Watershed, 256 Marginal St. in East Boston, 02128. It is the fourth annual edition, according to the listing.

title: Fenway Studios Opens Its Doors to More Than 25 Artists This Weekend
dek: Through Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5:00 p.m., at Fenway Studios, 30 Ipswich Street, in the 1905 National Historic Landmark building.
body: Fenway Studios' Open Studios Weekend Celebration runs from 11:00 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, to 5:00 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 8. Visitors can meet more than 25 artists, view their work and tour the studios in the 1905 building, which is a National Historic Landmark.
## A look inside

Open studios let visitors see where the work is made as well as the finished pieces, and the listing says they can see the work of more than 25 artists in one weekend. The listing describes the weekend as a chance to meet local artists in their own spaces, and it calls it an annual event.
## A food drive

The 18th annual food drive benefits The Home For Little Wanderers and runs alongside the open studios, so visitors can bring donations when they visit. The listing asks visitors to bring Thanksgiving-style donations, including stuffing, gravy, cranberry sauce, canned yams, peas or carrots, cake and pudding mixes, chocolate candies and cookies.
## Admission

The 1905 building is listed as a National Historic Landmark, so the weekend also offers a look at a historic building as well as the artists. The listing shows admission at no charge, so the weekend is open to anyone who wants to walk through the building and meet the artists.

title: 48 Cellos Honor Pablo Casals in Roxbury, Nov. 8
dek: Sunday, Nov. 8 at 3 p.m. at the Roxbury Community College Media Arts Center, marking Casals's 150th birthday, with no charge admission.
body: Forty-eight cellists will fill the stage at Roxbury Community College on Sunday afternoon, Nov. 8, to celebrate the 150th birthday of Pablo Casals. The Catalan cellist is remembered by the presenters as a cellist and humanitarian, and this concert gives his music a full, rich sound.
## The ensemble

The All-Cello Orchestra brings together students and faculty from Berklee, Boston Conservatory at Berklee, Boston University, Longy School of Music and New England Conservatory. Eugene Friesen conducts. Vivo Performing Arts presents the concert, with thanks to Lizbeth and George Krupp for their leadership of its Roxbury programming.
## The program

The program moves from France to Brazil and back to Catalonia. It includes Gabriel Faure's Pie Jesu from the Requiem, and Villa-Lobos's Bachianas Brasileiras No. 5, with the soprano Nicole DiPasquale. Several works are by Casals himself, among them Nigra Sum, El cant dels ocells (Bird Song), Sant Marti del Canigo and a Sardana for cello orchestra. A newer piece by Mike Block, When the Birds Sing Along in the Morning, draws on Casals's memoir Joys and Sorrows.
## Admission and details

The concert starts at 3 p.m., with a pre-show talk at 2:15 p.m. Admission is no charge, and the event page recommends the concert for ages 4 and up. The page links to a parking and accessibility page for the Media Arts Center, rather than printing a street address, so check that page before you go. Reminders can be requested from the event page.

The page describes the cello's range as one that overlaps with the human voice, which is part of what makes forty-eight of them sound so moving together. It is a rare chance to hear a whole orchestra of cellos, and a fine afternoon for music lovers of every age.

title: The 48th Boston International Antiquarian Book Fair Opens at the Hynes
dek: Friday, November 6 through Sunday, November 8 at the Hynes Convention Center in Back Bay, with about 110 rare book dealers.
body: The 48th Boston International Antiquarian Book Fair opens on Friday, November 6, at the Hynes Convention Center in Back Bay and runs through Sunday, November 8. About 110 rare book dealers are bringing first editions, manuscripts, maps and autographs, and they travel to Boston from the Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Serbia, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and 24 states.

Hours are 4 to 8 p.m. on Friday, noon to 7 p.m. on Saturday and 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Sunday. A Friday ticket costs $25 and is good for all three days, Saturday is $15 and Sunday is $10. Students and children 12 and under are admitted at no charge, and librarians and staff of nonprofit cultural institutions can register in advance with an organizational email address.
## For new collectors

The fair is a good place to start. The dealers have set aside "Discovery" items priced at $100 or less for people who are just beginning to collect, so a visit can be as much a lesson as a shopping trip. A walk along the aisles puts handwritten pages and early printed books in front of you that are rarely seen outside a museum.
Check the fair's own pages before you go for the current dealer list and any schedule changes.

title: Boston Lyric Opera Opens 'A Streetcar Named Desire' This Week
dek: Thursday, Nov. 5 and Friday, Nov. 6 at 7:30 p.m. and Sunday, Nov. 8 at 3 p.m. at the Emerson Cutler Majestic Theatre on Tremont Street.
body: Boston Lyric Opera opens André Previn's A Streetcar Named Desire at the Emerson Cutler Majestic Theatre this week, with performances on Thursday, November 5 and Friday, November 6 at 7:30 p.m. and a matinee on Sunday, November 8 at 3 p.m. The opera sets a libretto by Philip Littell to Tennessee Williams' Pulitzer Prize-winning play. This production is a new co-production with Opera Theatre of Saint Louis and is sung in English with English supertitles.
## A Summer in New Orleans

The story unfolds during a sweltering New Orleans summer. Blanche DuBois moves in with her sister Stella and brother-in-law Stanley, and her romantic view of the past meets his blunt realism. Previn's score gives that meeting a lyrical voice, which makes the opera a fine introduction for anyone who knows Williams' play and for anyone who has never seen it.
## The Company
Daniela Candillari conducts, and Patricia Racette directs. Brittany Renee sings Blanche, Angela Yam sings Stella, Thomas Glass sings Stanley and Brenton Ryan sings Mitch.
## Performances and Tickets

The Emerson Cutler Majestic Theatre is at 219 Tremont Street in Boston. Tickets are sold through Boston Lyric Opera's online ticketing page, and the company also offers a general ticketing link for the rest of its season. Arrive a few minutes early to find your seat before the performance begins.

title: Troy Roberts Quartet Plays Arrow Street Arts Tonight, Nov. 9
dek: Monday, Nov. 9, at The Studio at Arrow Street Arts, 2 Arrow Street in Cambridge, with doors at 6:30 PM and music at 7:30 PM.
body: Troy Roberts, a GRAMMY-nominated saxophonist based in New York City, brings his quartet to Cambridge tonight for a jazz evening at The Studio at Arrow Street Arts. Roberts, an Australian immigrant, is a prolific bandleader with sixteen releases to his name, and he has recorded with artists including Joey DeFrancesco, Van Morrison and Kurt Elling.

His latest album is Green Lights, which features John Patitucci, Paul Bollenback and Jimmy Macbride. Tonight's lineup is Roberts on saxophone, Devin Thai on piano, Lois Majors on bass and Austin McMahon on drums.
## The evening

The show is presented by the New England Jazz Collaborative with Arrow Street Arts. Doors open at 6:30 PM, and the music runs from 7:30 to 9:30 PM, according to the event page. The Studio is at 2 Arrow Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so the concert suits a weeknight outing for anyone who wants a small room and a full quartet sound.
## Tickets

Tickets are sold through the event page on HappeningNext. Only digital tickets are accepted, so keep your ticket on your phone, because printed barcodes will not scan. The page does not list a price, so use the Find Tickets button on the event page for current pricing and availability.

title: Jazz Composers Alliance Orchestra Plays Four Berklee Faculty Composers
dek: Monday, Nov. 9 at 8 p.m. at the Berklee Performance Center, with music by four Berklee faculty composers.
body: The Jazz Composers Alliance Orchestra plays the Berklee Performance Center on Monday, November 9, at 8 p.m. The program presents music by four Berklee faculty composers: Bob Pilkington, Dave Harris, Mimi Rabson and Darrell Katz.
## A Familiar Address

The orchestra has played this hall before. The group's own website lists a November 2025 concert at the Berklee Performance Center on Massachusetts Avenue, so this evening continues a relationship between the ensemble and the college's main stage.
## The Music

The listing does not name individual pieces, so the evening is best understood as a showcase of how four composers who teach at Berklee write for a large jazz ensemble. Listeners who enjoy big-band writing, with composed sections and improvised solos, will find this a natural fit.
## Tickets

Tickets are sold through Etix. Check the Etix link for current prices. The Berklee box office is at 136 Massachusetts Avenue and can be reached at 617-747-2261 or boxoffice@berklee.edu to confirm hours.
